interactions.teaches: A fixed nominal debt becomes harder to pay when the debtor’s crop price falls.
interactions.studentAction: Choose 1891–1894 and compare wheat price with the bushels required to gross a fixed illustrative $500.
interactions.feedback: The price and required bushels update while the $500 block stays fixed.
interactions.staticFallback: Four historical year/price/bushel values remain readable in the content and can be shown simultaneously when motion is reduced.
interactions.identityFit: The interaction makes the title’s central idea physical: one number moves and the other refuses to.

interactions.teaches: Higher western freight rates and lower western traffic density can both be true.
interactions.studentAction: Move through 1890–1895 and inspect both indexed measures against national average = 100.
interactions.feedback: Both measures update together; the interpretation keeps the farmer and railroad claims in the same field.
interactions.staticFallback: An accessible data table provides all six years and both measures.
interactions.identityFit: It prevents a cartoon villain by forcing the evidence to stay paired.

interactions.teaches: Interstate rail commerce created a regulatory problem larger than one state.
interactions.studentAction: Move a shipment from intrastate regulation through the Wabash interstate gap and then apply the 1887 federal layer.
interactions.feedback: Train position, authority label, and explanation change at each stage.
interactions.staticFallback: The three stage buttons and explanatory text remain complete without animation.
interactions.identityFit: The railroad keeps moving while legal authority changes underneath it.

interactions.teaches: The Omaha Platform connected separate economic grievances to proposed changes in national rules.
interactions.studentAction: Open six grievance planks to reveal the associated Populist demand.
interactions.feedback: Each plank exposes a grievance-to-policy relationship and the connected-count rises.
interactions.staticFallback: Every grievance and policy pair is present in semantic buttons and visible when expanded.
interactions.identityFit: Convergence turns scattered kitchen-table problems into a national political mechanism.

interactions.teaches: Debtors, creditors, and wage workers can rationally want different outcomes from inflation and monetary expansion.
interactions.studentAction: Switch among an indebted farmer, a creditor/banker, and a wage worker.
interactions.feedback: The same proposed monetary change is explained from each position without declaring one universally correct.
interactions.staticFallback: All three perspective buttons expose text and work without animation.
interactions.identityFit: Money behaves as a relationship between people rather than a good/evil coin graphic.

interactions.teaches: Backing Bryan in 1896 offered Populists more scale while making independent party identity harder to preserve.
interactions.studentAction: Compare staying independent with fusing behind Bryan.
interactions.feedback: The two political streams change relative emphasis and the strategic tradeoff is stated.
interactions.staticFallback: Both choices have complete textual explanations.
interactions.identityFit: Fusion is represented as two political currents combining, not as a candidate trivia question.

interactions.teaches: Some Populist demands later entered mainstream law while other major demands did not.
interactions.studentAction: Inspect the final ledger of moved and unmoved demands.
interactions.feedback: Each later reform names what changed and avoids equating partial echoes with total Populist victory.
interactions.staticFallback: Semantic cards present all outcomes with text labels, not color alone.
interactions.identityFit: The ending returns to the lesson’s core language of numbers and rules that moved or did not.
